minutes.headline: Parks Commission adopted portable toilet and dumpster policies; schools agreed to waive field fees pending a policy rewrite.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed priorities for a Marshall Park master plan RFP, then drafted and adopted policies on portable toilets and dumpsters placed on park land. It discussed rescinding the verbal reciprocal field-use agreement with the schools; with the school committee chair and superintendent present, the sides agreed to keep it, have the school committee waive fees as needed, and revise school policy. Invasive plants, open space parcels and a skate park inquiry were also raised.

budget_items.what_was_said: A soccer camp was cancelled after the schools quoted an hourly field charge for a for-profit group.

decisions.decision: The chair will ask the assistant town manager to help draft the Marshall Park RFP, starting from survey, existing-conditions assessment, new and improved recreation areas, and ask when to submit the priority list.

Parks and school officials agreed the school committee would discuss waiving field fees at its August meeting and as needed until policy is revised, with the policy revision likely finishing by late October.
The chair will ask Little League to a meeting in August or September, with the DPW director, to discuss field treatment.
The next meeting is set for July 28, with a dog policy and invasive plants on the agenda.

what_happened.line: The commission voted by roll call to adopt a portable sanitation facilities policy, with a title added to the text as written.
The commission voted by roll call to accept a drafted dumpster policy for dumpsters placed on park land.
With the school committee chair and superintendent present, the sides kept the verbal field-use agreement; the school committee would discuss waiving field fees in August.
The chair will ask the assistant town manager to help draft a Marshall Park master plan RFP, and ask when the priority list is due.
The next meeting is set for July 28, with a dog policy and invasive plants on the agenda.

why_it_matters: Rules on portable toilets and dumpsters now govern what can be placed on town park land, and members said current fees would not cover three portable units, so field and park user fees may need to change.
Whether school fields are charged for use depends on a verbal agreement with the schools and a school policy still being revised, so youth groups and camps may face fees until that is settled.
